justification: Design/UX round 1 for /csharp-dotnet/strings-and-unicode/ (words=2290, code=18, fig=1, h1=1, 7 sections). Verified with `node tools/verify-page.mjs --drafts /csharp-dotnet/strings-and-unicode/` run from the worktree in PowerShell: PASS, Lighthouse 100/100/100/100 (a clean serial run, no other jobs running), report.json shows 0 console errors, 0 console warnings, 0 broken links (28 internal, 8 external, all resolved), mobileOverflowPx 0, placeholders [] (the byline resolved to the linked 'Computer Science Guide' author, so even the usually-expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder failure is absent). Read every desktop-light part (01-08), every mobile-dark part (01-12), the mobile-light fold plus parts 06-07 (the figure and comparison-output block), and desktop-dark fold plus parts 03-04 (the figure in dark mode). Against the two Microsoft Learn pages this article leans on hardest for its central claims (character-encoding-introduction, best-practices-strings) -- both plain prose with a couple of code snippets, no diagrams, no dark theme, no interactive/collapsed exercises -- this article is well ahead on illustration and on letting a reader run the surprising cases themselves rather than take the docs' word for it. Structure follows the plan's shape I (illustrative/exploratory) outline exactly: immutability/interning -> StringBuilder cost measured -> UTF-16/surrogate pairs (with the required diagram) -> the three counting APIs -> Rune -> culture-sensitive comparison (Turkish-I) -> Span<char>, each section building on the last via the opening emoji-length hook. Heading hierarchy is clean: one h1, seven flat h2 sections matching 'On this page' exactly, no skipped levels. Rhythm is good throughout -- no code block runs more than one output block before returning to explanatory prose, and every output panel is immediately followed by a paragraph that names what changed and why. The two exercises (a mid-article 'measure it' after the concat benchmark, a 'find the bug' after the Turkish-I pitfall) are both well-formed per WRITER_GUIDE section 4: correct four-colon/three-colon nesting, solutions collapsed with no output visible above the fold in any of the screenshots checked, and neither gives away its answer in the prompt. The single :::pitfall callout is used exactly as WRITER_GUIDE describes it (a mistake people commonly make -- treating CurrentCulture as test-only) and is not overused elsewhere. Code fences all use the correct `csharp run id=...` / `text output` convention with the output block directly after its program every time, matching tools/run-code.mjs; the char/Rune/text-element comparison data is deliberately kept inside a program's `text output` panel rather than a GFM table, which sidesteps the wide-comparison-table mobile risk entirely -- confirmed on both mobile screenshots, all four columns (sample/Len/Rune/Elem) sit comfortably inside the 40-column budget with no fade or wrap. No code line clips an operative token on phone width in any block checked; the one long line with a boilerplate tail (the Old Italic `string word = "ok\U00010330\U00010331";` declaration and the flag-emoji samples-array entry) only cuts a trailing comment or a hex escape the prose doesn't ask the reader to read off the screen. The required diagram (Figure 1, code-unit vs code-point vs grapheme-cluster using the JP flag emoji) is well executed: viewBox 360x280 (portrait, well under the 360 budget so it never scrolls at 390px), no blank lines anywhere inside the `<figure>` (checked the raw markdown directly, lines 160-193 are contiguous), correct `role="img"` plus unique `<title>`/`<desc>` pair, theme-correct in both light and dark (the d-box-accent/d-box/d-box-2 classes switch cleanly, confirmed in desktop-dark part03 and mobile-dark part06), and it genuinely clarifies rather than decorates: it is the visual anchor the next two sections (three counting APIs, Rune) both refer back to. Two things hold this back from 8.5+: first, CONTENT_PLAN.md section 7 requires 'every article' to carry '3-6 exercises with solutions,' and this article has only 2 -- one short of the minimum, so the reading-rhythm checkpoint the rubric cares about is thinner than the plan requires for an article this long (2290 words, 7 sections). Second, the flag emoji that Figure 1's box and caption both name ('The flag emoji "🇯🇵"') renders as the plain letters 'JP' rather than a flag pictograph in every screenshot checked -- light, dark, mobile and desktop alike -- because the two regional-indicator code points fall back to their letter glyphs on this rendering stack. The diagram still works logically (the boxes, arrows and hex code-unit values are all correct and legible), but the visual hook the caption leans on ('the flag emoji') is not actually a flag for a real share of readers on the same stack, which is a real, verifiable gap between what the caption promises and what the drawing shows.

issues.location: Whole article -- 2 `::::exercise` blocks total (line 121 'Measure it', line 297 'Find the bug'), checked against all 7 h2 sections and all 12 mobile-dark parts
issues.problem: CONTENT_PLAN.md section 7 states plainly: 'Every article carries: at least one original diagram unless marked (no diagram needed), runnable code, 3-6 exercises with solutions, and a sources list.' This article has the diagram, the runnable code and the sources, but only 2 exercises against a 3-6 minimum. Both existing exercises are well-placed and well-formed, but a 2290-word, 7-section article with this many distinct testable claims (interning, the O(n^2) vs O(n) cost shape, three different counting APIs, Rune-vs-char classification, ordinal vs culture comparison, allocation-free slicing) has room for at least one more checkpoint without padding.
issues.fixLooksLike: Add at least one more `::::exercise[...]` block with a collapsed `:::solution` per WRITER_GUIDE section 4, placed mid-section rather than appended at the end (EDITORIAL_BRIEF's 'vary the ending' rule, which this article already otherwise respects by not ending on an 'Exercises' heading). Natural spots that are not yet exercises: a predict-the-output on the three-counts comparison table (e.g. what would a new sample with a ZWJ emoji sequence report for Len/Rune/Elem), or an extend-it on the Span<char> parser (e.g. handle a reading with no trailing unit suffix).

issues.location: Figure 1 ("What .Length is actually counting" section) -- the top box and the figcaption both name the JP flag emoji; confirmed in desktop-light part03, desktop-dark part03, mobile-light part07, mobile-dark part06
issues.problem: The SVG text element and the figcaption both render the two regional-indicator code points as the plain letters 'JP' rather than a flag pictograph, in every theme/width combination captured. The rest of the diagram (the code-point and code-unit rows, the hex values, the arrows) is unaffected and remains correct and legible, but the caption's framing ('The flag emoji "🇯🇵" is one grapheme cluster...') describes a visual the reader does not actually see on this rendering stack, which is a real gap between what is promised and what is drawn, not just a font nicety -- a flag is the whole visual hook for why this example was chosen over a plainer surrogate-pair case.
issues.fixLooksLike: Either accept it (the boxes and hex breakdown still teach the concept correctly without the pictograph) or verify how the flag renders in the site's actual deployed font stack across common reader platforms; if it is inconsistent site-wide, this is a shared rendering concern for tools/verify-page.mjs's screenshot environment and any other article using regional-indicator emoji, not specific to this article's markup, so it may belong in docs/INTEGRATOR_REQUESTS.md rather than a per-article fix.
